sections.currentVisual: [Verified by reading] TWO moving things today. (1) Backdrop: HeroAtmosphere.tsx - one drei <ScreenQuad> with a hand-written GLSL fragment program (atmosphere.glsl.ts): 4-octave value-noise fbm far + mid layers, a 3-octave ridged near layer stretched along a beam axis plus radial light shafts (both only when uQuality=1, i.e. canvas width >= 900 px, HeroAtmosphere.tsx:201), a sparse hash starfield, one key light high-left at (-0.62, 0.40), vignette, highlight shoulder, 1.8% grain; final colour is mix(uInk, uLight, luma) with uInk=PALETTE.ink900 #0A0B0D and uLight=PALETTE.white #F4F6FA so it is achromatic by construction. Pointer parallax (uPointer*0.055) and page-scroll parallax (uScroll*-0.12) are CPU-lerped (delta*1.6 / delta*1.4); entrance is uIntensity += delta*0.65 (~1.5 s fade). Cost per glsl comment: 16 noise lookups/pixel at up to 1.75x DPR; R3F+three arrive in a separate chunk (GLCanvas.tsx comment cites 132 kB kept off the critical path); dpr [1,1.75], antialias on, stencil off, powerPreference high-performance. Mount gates (Scene.tsx:91): WebGL probe 'supported' (software rasterisers such as SwiftShader rejected unless ?gl=force, useGLCapability.ts:179-187) AND prefers-reduced-motion not matched AND slot within rootMargin 50% AND window load + requestIdleCallback fired. (2) Type entrance: pure CSS `heroRise` (opacity 0->1, translateY 14px->0), duration --motion-cine 900 ms, easing --motion-ease-emphasized, delay = --step * --stagger(90 ms) + 120 ms across seven --step values 0..6 (Hero.module.css:94-115, Hero.tsx:39-98). Reduced-motion path: Scene never mounts (no canvas), backdrop is the CSS `.stage` gradient (radial rgb(27 29 35/0.85) at 22% 18% over linear ink-900 -> ink-800 -> ink-900, Hero.module.css:76-83); entrance swaps to `heroFade` 320 ms linear, delay --step*40 ms (Hero.module.css:395-416). No-WebGL path: identical to reduced-motion backdrop; every word is server-rendered. [Verified live 2026-09-04 via host CDP 127.0.0.1:9222 at 1440x900 on https://forgotten-mistory.web.app] #hero canvas count 0 (host Chrome is SwiftShader, expected), h1 class Hero_name__vovn8, .hero-title absent, .avatar-placeholder absent, 0 gold-painted elements in #hero.

sections.cinematicOpportunity: ONE visual, 'The ledger drawn': make the three graded figures the animation instead of the mood. On first paint the caliper jaws (white hairlines, Caliper.module.css geometry) close onto each value in sequence - ~92%, $5M+, 10k+ - while the provenance line prints beneath in mono grey, and the atmosphere's single high-left key light rakes once across the ledger as each pair of jaws closes (drive uIntensity/lightPos from the same --step clock so shader and type share one beat). The existing seven-step type rise is folded into that one sequence, so the hero owns one choreography, not two. Palette: black ground, white type and hairlines, grey provenance; gold NONE unless a figure is upgraded to `sourced` with a public methodology (CT-10 forbids it for these three; prime directive 3 forbids it anyway) - so the hero stays black/white by design and the gold budget is spent later on the page. If the Owner instead chooses the hero video avatar as the hero's one moving thing, the atmosphere must go static and the type rise become a plain fade - a portrait video + a shader + a seven-step rise is three animations, and the portrait must be graded black-and-white (see sharedFindings for the twelve missing CSS classes, fold/LCP/baseline consequences and the tests that must be written first).

sections.story: The ten dimensions Vikram's own job-fit engine (aether-job-career-agent, apps/api/app/routers/jobs.py) scores a candidate on, answered about himself with evidence but deliberately with NO scores (about.ts:66-70; TC-ABOUT-03 fails on any percentage/x-of-10/meter). The instrument enacts that refusal: a face with no needle and no magnitude, seven closed sectors for what the engine measures from the candidate, three open hatched sectors for what it measures from the role (same hatch as the open Caliper, so the mark is learned once). Turning the bezel to bring the read dimension to the index is a reading aid. The visual carries the argument correctly but not as a story: at rest it reads '--' / 'NO SCORES' and does nothing until hovered; on a phone (no hover, static, 14rem) the dial never turns unless an item receives focus; there is no entrance, no sequence and no scroll-driven state, so a reader who does not hover sees a static dial beside a list.

sections.cinematicOpportunity: ONE visual, 'The face wakes': a scroll-triggered sequence on the existing SVG (IntersectionObserver on `.instrumentStage`, once). Bezel ticks and hub ring fade in; the ten sectors light in engine order 01->10 on a 90 ms stagger, the seven candidate sectors filling white-grey and the three role sectors hatching in rather than filling; the rose then sweeps one full turn and settles on 01 with the hub reading '01 / ANSWERED'; from there the existing hover/focus indexing takes over. Add scroll-indexing: as the reader scrolls the list, the item nearest the viewport centre becomes `active` (About.tsx already owns the state), so the dial turns for phones, keyboard-less readers and screen-recorded demos - the instrument then narrates the list instead of waiting for a pointer. Palette: black ground, --white/--steel hairlines, grey; gold NONE (no dimension here is sourced; keep the index white - do not 'restore' the gold the stale comment describes). Reduced motion: the same sequence as an opacity-only stagger (satisfies RM-1..3; stroke-dashoffset drawing is banned under reduce by RM-3 so use opacity there), rose snaps to the active sector (already), and delete the `transition: none` blocks in About.module.css:255-261 / Compass.module.css:490-498 so colour transitions survive (RM-4) - globals.css:941-957 already removes transform from transition-property. Header comment ('The scene sits behind it and draws the same spans in space') describes the abandoned 3D-bars scene; strata.glsl.ts:2-15 and CareerStrata.tsx:10-13 state the opposite (texture, not data). Doc drift on the very point the shader was rewritten over.

`scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })` on chart-row click animates the scroll even when prefers-reduced-motion is set: the `behavior` option takes precedence over CSS scroll-behavior, so the `html { scroll-behavior: auto !important }` guard at globals.css:942-944 does not apply to this call.
defects.evidence: Experience.tsx:105-111; globals.css:941-944. Behaviour-precedence from CSSOM View spec, not measured here.

defects.description: At <=760 px `.trackYears { display: none }` removes the duration readout, so on a phone a bar's length is the only statement of its duration and the 'no published figure' roles show a bar with no number at all; the axis then carries the whole claim - and the axis is the misaligned element (defect 1).

NOW is hard-coded to September 2026 (2026 + 8/12) by design; the 'now' tick and the open ATO bar freeze there until the constant is edited with the CV. Stated in the file; recorded so the next run does not 'fix' it with new Date().

sections.cinematicOpportunity: ONE visual, 'Drawn to scale': retire the strata backdrop (it encodes nothing and costs a GL context) and make the chart itself the animation. On first intersection the axis rule draws left to right from 2010 to now; then the eight bars extend from their start year at one constant px-per-year rate, so the ANZ bar visibly takes eight times longer to arrive than the ten-month NAB bar - the duration IS the animation and restates the section's one claim; each bar ends by fading in its year readout, and for the three roles with a headline figure the caliper jaws close beneath as the bar completes while the five open brackets stay dashed; a hairline 'now' cursor holds at the right edge. Hover, focus, click and the accordion are unchanged. Palette: black ground, --white bars, --ink-300/--mist-400 readouts; gold NONE (no figure here has a published methodology; -38% is explicitly simulated). Reduced motion: bars pre-drawn at full width with an opacity-only stagger (RM-1), colour transitions kept by deleting Experience.module.css:434-442 (RM-4), no width/transform animation (RM-3). No-WebGL: identical - it is CSS on the existing DOM bars (scaleX from transform-origin left under no-preference). Prerequisite: fix the axis margin (defect 1) first, and add a Playwright assertion that each axis tick centre is within 2 px of its gridline plus a VIS baseline for #experience, or the bars will animate onto the wrong ticks.

[Verified] Gold-as-claim across the three sections: a live CDP sweep of color/backgroundColor/border colours/fill/stroke plus ::before/::after on every element of #hero, #about and #experience found 0 elements painted in any of the four sanctioned golds. Reason: every figure in these sections is Caliper 'self-reported' (hero ledger x3, ato/independent/anz headlines) or 'open' (three role-side dimensions, five roles with no published figure), and the only gold path is Caliper 'sourced' (Caliper.module.css:71-84).
